advisory.finding: The new foreign-path classification logic in _resolve_conflicted_apply (path_is_foreign_to_branch → logger.warning → discard_unmerged_paths(foreign) with os.remove) is never exercised by the new test. The stash COMMIT is built from the tracker's own dirty tree (shared.txt, untouched.txt), both branch-tracked, so the only conflicted path on apply is tracked ('regenerable') and the 'foreign' bucket is always empty. The src/leak.py and src/raced.py files live in the separate refs/stash entries and never reach the apply, so assertions #1 pass without the classification/removal branch ever running. A regression that mis-classified a foreign conflicted path (e.g. path_is_foreign_to_branch returning the wrong bucket, or discard_unmerged_paths failing to remove) would not be caught.
scenarios: A conflicted-apply where a stranded UU path is genuinely foreign (untracked on the tickets branch) — the branch the diff was written to add
